The Azure Workload Identity Operator is installed in {{ .Release.Namespace }}.

Verify both controllers and the validating webhook:

  kubectl get deployments,pods -n {{ .Release.Namespace }}
  kubectl get validatingwebhookconfiguration azure-workload-identity-operator-validating-webhook-configuration
{{- if .Values.azureWorkloadIdentityWebhook.enabled }}
  kubectl get deployments,pods -n {{ .Values.azureWorkloadIdentityWebhook.namespaceOverride }}
  kubectl get mutatingwebhookconfiguration azure-wi-webhook-mutating-webhook-configuration
{{- end }}

The chart retains its CRDs and Azure-scope identity ConfigMap during uninstall.
Delete them manually only after all custom resources have been removed or
intentionally abandoned.

This chart uses stable, cluster-wide resource names and supports one release
per cluster. Moving the release to another namespace is a migration.
